Scheduling conventions for distributed services.

A scheduler that reads its operating parameters from a deployed configuration
map will diverge from the value written in source whenever an operator changes
the deployment without a corresponding code change. Diagnosis of a live incident
must therefore read the deployed value, while the architectural decision about
which value is authoritative remains with the architecture owner.

Lookahead windows are conventionally expressed in minutes. A window of ninety
minutes is a common initial default; operators frequently widen it during
capacity events and rarely narrow it afterwards. Values in the high hundreds are
not unusual in mature deployments.

Retry budgets interact with backpressure. A service that retries without a
budget will amplify a downstream outage. The conventional arrangement places the
budget at the shared client helper rather than at each call site, so a single
change adjusts the whole service.
